A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DisTaC research. Their main text, appendices, equations, algorithms, tables and figures are readable and can be matched despite reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original CLIP model-merging experiments on eight vision tasks, including performance comparisons, training curves, calibration experiments and scaling analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original vision experiments and adds comparator results, data-sensitivity experiments, computational measurements and GLUE evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same scaled initialization, teacher-student distillation, asymmetric temperatures and regularization around the initialization. The NLP evaluations introduce no documented change to DisTaC's procedure.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix E.7 adds language evaluations on four GLUE tasks: CoLA, MRPC, RTE and SST-2. Appendix E.5 also adds Gaussian-blurred inputs during distillation, extending input-condition coverage. The eight vision tasks and existing calibration scenarios remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands the evaluated merging methods from four to seven by adding EMR-Merging, Iso-CTS and WUDI-Merging, each with and without DisTaC. Tables 3–4 additionally introduce Distill-from-Pretrained as a comparison. Table 6 extends the original four merging comparators to NLP.

E3.justification: The original vision protocol remains unchanged. Added experiments introduce 100–500 unlabeled samples per class, relative accuracy against full-data or clean-data performance, and Gaussian blur with kernel size 5 and three intensity ranges. NLP evaluation introduces RoBERTa-base, RoBERTa-large and Llama2-7b configurations.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.5 tests sensitivity to unlabeled-data quantity and blur corruption, using pretrained initialization as a control to investigate the benefit of DisTaC's initialization. The existing layer-wise norm, calibration, vector-scaling and scaling-only analyses are retained from v1 Appendix C.

E5.justification: Figure 2 retains the same mean and one-standard-deviation reporting across eight tasks. v2 adds no seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals or significance tests; its new tables report point estimates.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 comparator scores and Table 2 results are retained, while v2 adds extensive vision, NLP, robustness and computational results. New comparisons include WUDI-Merging's low-confidence ViT-L-14 accuracy of 28.0 without versus 91.6 with DisTaC, and Table 6's RoBERTa-large task-arithmetic norm-mismatch normalized scores of 58.1 versus 80.5. Exceptions also appear: Iso-CTS low-confidence ViT-B-32 accuracy decreases from 72.5 to 69.0 with DisTaC.

T1.justification: v1 Section 3.1's approximate cosine argument becomes Proposition 1 with exact identities, quantitative bounds and a proof in new Appendix B. The calibration derivation is largely retained from v1 Appendix A as v2 Appendix C; Theorem 1 becomes Proposition 2 with a more explicit sign condition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: norm disparity and low confidence impair merging, distillation conditions task vectors, and shrinking vectors followed by post-merge calibration is preferable. The added experiments supply further evidence without redefining these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking robustness to scaled initialization and teacher-based noise filtering, claims vision-language generalization, and introduces explicit applicability and data-access limitations. However, Section 8's vision-only limitation contradicts Appendix E.7, and its claim of over 96% performance under scarce or shifted data exceeds entries of 83.9% and 91.7% in Tables 3–4.

D1.justification: v2 adds data-size and blur specifications plus Table 5's profiling details: two A100 GPUs, batch size 64 per device, approximately 3.2 seconds for 500 steps excluding evaluation, and 7.1 GB peak memory. Existing vision hyperparameters and the code-access statement are retained. Detailed NLP training and metric specifications remain limited.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for the new comparators and NLP resources, brief MAP and DOGE discussions, and a theoretical connection in Section 6.1. v1's Chat Vector reference is removed; the newly cited EMR-Merging is a different Huang et al. 2024 work. The central positioning of DisTaC remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative remain intact. Related work moves from Section 7 to Appendix A, the calibration appendix is condensed and regrouped, and a limitations section is added. Author, conference-header and acknowledgment text also changes.

P2.justification: Table 1 substantially expands its comparator rows, and new Tables 3–6 display data-size sensitivity, blur robustness, computational cost and NLP results. The document adopts conference typography and reflows existing displays, including relocating Figure 7. Figures 1–8 and Table 2 retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's vision-only evidence and step-count efficiency discussion, v2 provides broader comparisons, language evaluations, data-sensitivity tests and measured computational costs. These strengthen support for generality and practicality. The net gain is limited by sparse NLP protocol documentation and unreconciled reporting: Section 8 contradicts the added language experiments and overstates robustness, while blanket improvement statements overlook counterexamples such as Iso-CTS in Table 1.
